mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-rate periods (t-test p > 0.05), or the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS does not exceed 2% for 10 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 50,000 and UNRATE < previous month
failure_condition: No significant correlation between PAYEMS growth and UNRATE declines in the 60-day window, or SPX 60-day returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.2% inflation-adjusted growth for two consecutive months indicates accelerating demand for goods and services, which elevates firm earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified growth period, or CPIAUCSL growth does not persist beyond the trigger window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in the ratio of orders to shipments (not directly observable here, but implied by INDPRO trend) suggests weakening supply chain capacity, which raises production costs and reduces profit margins, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly decline of > 5% for two months
failure_condition: INDPRO does not exhibit the predicted decline in two consecutive months, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 1%, it signals a shift to accommodative policy, lowering real interest rates and increasing the present value of future equities, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days in a post-recession environment.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward returns during the easing phase (p > 0.05), or the 3-month MA does not cross below 1% as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies, so this sketch is invalid under the given catalog - therefore will not be included) - instead, we use PAYEMS and UNRATE interaction to capture labor market tightness. When job openings (implied by high PAYEMS and low UNRATE) increase, firms expand hiring and investment, pushing S&P 500 returns positive over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day returns during high PAYEMS/low UNRATE periods (p > 0.05), or the interaction term is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer confidence proxies (none available in the provided catalog - so this sketch is invalid) - instead, using INDPRO as a proxy for supply conditions, a sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of over 2% for three months indicates deteriorating manufacturing capacity, which suppresses earnings growth and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO does not decline as predicted, or 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 2% for 4 consecutive months), the lower real interest rate environment increases the present value of equity cash flows, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day forward returns during the easing period (p > 0.05), or the FEDFUNDS threshold is not met for 4 consecutive months.
